clinical_observations.content: Sabrina participated in an in-clinic evaluation with her mother present. She exhibited a generally cheerful and cooperative demeanor; however, her attention span was inconsistent, requiring frequent redirection. Muscle tone was observed to be within normal limits, and range of motion was age-appropriate. Sabrina engaged willingly in structured activities but often needed maximal verbal and visual cues to sustain participation, whereas self-directed activities heightened distractibility. During manual dexterity assessments, Sabrina's fine motor coordination was observed to be delayed, necessitating hand-over-hand assistance to complete tasks. Throughout the evaluation, Sabrina's response to instructions varied, suggesting a limited ability to self-regulate. Consequently, standard testing conditions were modified to encompass breaks and support task participation, which nonetheless affected the validity of test scores.
